questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English-speaking country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy- it was all provided via zoom presentations and e-mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The host institution found it for me- expensive but saved me from the stress of finding it myself, so I do think that was the correct choice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My accommodation was "kollegie" style with rented rooms and a shared living room and kitchen- technically not living on campus but found via the host institution. This will be expensive, but the easiest way to meet other students, so be friendly from day one.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Quite easy- they sent some emails with links I think and how-tos. I don't actually remember the specifics but this means it must have been easy enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were some zoom meetings where some of the registration was discussed I think, so great to watch those. There were two main people from my host institution that were supposed to be able to answer any questions/emails- I didn't personally use this help and heard that it could take several weeks to get an answer, but that help is there. A WhatsApp group for Erasmus students was set up during one of the zoom meetings in the chat, and that was very helpful to join and hear what kinds of issues others were having and how to resolve them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly successful- there were issues as the timetable isn't released until right before the start of the semester, so last minute I had to switch out some classes so that there wouldn't be several at the same time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration is a little funky at UCC, so you can change classes a while after the semester already has begun- this is very helpful, so try out a few classes and don't be afraid to drop it and chose another.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My classes were all designed for 2nd or 3rd year students in their undergrad (3 classes for 2nd year and 3 classes for 3rd year).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had almost all lecture-style classes as opposed to seminar-style or lab-style (even my lab-style class was taught as a lecture basically).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: AY2008 The biology of being human; EV2003 Practical data analysis and research skills; GG2014 Geography of tourism; GG3037 Geography of heritage; GG3041 Environmental remote sensing; GG3058 Environmental geography

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: AY2008 The biology of being human: super nice professor, fun/interesting class, other kind students during my semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee/tea at UCC was more expensive than KU; food wasn't as expensive as I expected (but still expensive); bus-fares are a set price (I just avoided using it in general because 1.9 euro pr short ride adds up); sending postcards was expensive (but I love to do it!)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Clubs (sports) and societies (clubs for people with similar hobbies or interests). There are a lot of different clubs and societies available and a whole fair around campus to talk to representatives from them to see if it's something for you.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join all the clubs and societies that remotely interest you and then just stick to the ones you like best! A really great way to meet people- everyone who goes is interested in talking about your shared interest and making friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the train to a nearby city (Cobh is super cute!). I had the privilege of having great flat mates and we did a road trip to Killarney and Dingle and this was really great (in the off season no less and this was fun to explore with no other tourists around). A tour bus is also an option- I did one to the Cliffs of Moher (avoid if you get car sick though!). Cork has a load to offer though- make sure you consistently do things so you don't have a huge to-do list of museums and sites to see right before going home.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and societies. Say hi to the person next to you in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing that stood out to me- perhaps brash jokes but you get used to it quickly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pretty laid-back people in general, even the professors.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join societies/clubs, make friends with your flatmates, say hi to the people sitting next to you in class
2. Do something every weekend: go to a museum, wander around Cork, take the train to Cobh, etc.
3. You have up to 6 classes at the same time, presumably with exams/essays due around the same times- start working on essays early even if you haven't necessarily covered all the topics of the class yet.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to do things alone- I went to societies/clubs alone and met people there, that is normal and what they're there for. Do sightseeing alone, don't wait for others. I met my best Cork friend later in the semester, so don't stop trying to make friends through the exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just being able to say I did it- I went and lived somewhere where I didn't know anyone beforehand and made some great memories.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting out of my comfort zone, having to do university from scratch and not knowing anyone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
